figures.caption: 圖：討論班費用途的班會
figures.description: 教室裡正在開班會。擔任主席的班長站在黑板旁主持討論；黑板上寫著「班費怎麼用？」，下面列出三個選項：一、買新的球類用品；二、期末辦班級聚餐；三、買書架和小盆栽布置教室。台下前排一個男生站起來發言，另外兩個同學舉著手等待發言；一個女生坐在旁邊，把大家的意見寫在筆記本上；導師坐在教室後方，安靜地聽著。

questions.stem: 提示：班上存了一筆班費，班會時大家正在討論要怎麼使用。請仔細看下面的圖片，寫一篇英文作文，文分兩段。第一段描述圖中班會討論的情形；第二段寫出你在班會中發言或參與討論的一次經驗，並提出你希望班費怎麼使用的簡單計畫與理由。

1.explanation_zh: 這一題有三個要求：第一段描述班會的情形（主席、黑板上的三個選項、發言與舉手的同學、做紀錄的同學、導師）；第二段先寫一次自己在班會發言或參與討論的經驗，再提出班費怎麼用的簡單計畫與理由。計畫要具體（買什麼、怎麼分工），理由至少兩個；可以從黑板上的選項挑一個，也可以提出自己的想法。
evidence: 第一段描述圖中班會討論的情形
提出你希望班費怎麼使用的簡單計畫與理由
1.strategy_zh: 第二段有兩個任務，先寫經驗（過去式），再用 If I could decide …, I would … 帶出計畫（would＋原形動詞），最後用 First、Second 列理由。
hints: 第一段：主席在做什麼、黑板上有哪三個選項、台下的同學在做什麼
第二段前半：Last …, I spoke at a class meeting … 寫一次經驗
第二段後半：If I could decide how to use our class fund, I would … 接兩個理由

moves.zh: 描述圖中班會討論的情形
寫出你在班會中發言或參與討論的一次經驗
提出你希望班費怎麼使用的簡單計畫與理由

content.focus_zh: 第一段寫出主席、選項與發言的同學；第二段要有一次參與班會的具體經驗，以及一個具體的班費計畫和至少兩個理由。

bands.descriptor_zh: 回應題目的每一項要求，主旨明確；用具體的事例、細節或親身經驗撐起每個重點。
大致回應題目，但有一項要求寫得單薄，或細節偏籠統、說服力不足。
漏掉題目的主要要求或主旨模糊，多數句子空泛、重複或偏離題目。
空白、離題、只抄題目，或內容少到無法判斷要說什麼。

organization.focus_zh: 第二段先經驗、後計畫，中間要有轉接句（例如「如果現在由我決定…」）；理由用 First、Second 列出，結尾回應班費的用途。

bands.descriptor_zh: 兩段分工清楚，各有主題句；句與句、段與段的銜接自然，轉承語用得恰當，篇幅分配合理。
段落大致分明，但有的地方跳接或重複，轉承語偏少或用得生硬。
重點排列混亂，前後句常接不起來，讀者不容易跟上。
看不出段落與順序，句子彼此無關。

grammar.focus_zh: 經驗用過去式；計畫用 would＋原形動詞（I would buy …）；If I could decide … 的時態要一致。

bands.descriptor_zh: 句子幾乎沒有文法、標點錯誤，能交替使用簡單句、複句與不同的句首。
偶有時態、單複數或標點錯誤，但讀得懂意思；句型變化有限。
錯誤多到常讓人誤解意思，句子結構常不完整。
幾乎沒有正確的句子，無法理解。

vocabulary.focus_zh: 班會、班費、發言、投票等說法（class meeting、class fund、give an opinion、vote for）要用對；避免一直重複 good。

bands.descriptor_zh: 用字精準、貼切，搭配自然，少有重複；拼字與大小寫幾乎全對。
字彙範圍偏窄、常重複同幾個字，偶有用字不當或拼錯，但不妨礙理解。
用錯字或拼錯字很多，常讓人看不懂。
幾乎每個字都用錯或拼錯，無法理解。

rubric.deductions_zh: 字數明顯不足（少於 100 個單詞）或沒有分成兩段，各扣總分 1 分；兩種情形同時發生只扣 1 分。離題或空白以 0 分計。

sentence_starters: The picture shows a class meeting about ...
Last semester, I spoke at a class meeting ...
If I could decide how to use our class fund, I would ...

model_texts.label: steady
model_texts.text:
The picture shows a class meeting about how to use the class fund. The class leader is standing next to the blackboard and leading the discussion. On the blackboard, there are three choices: buying new balls, having a class party, and buying a bookshelf with some plants. In the front row, a boy is standing up and giving his opinion. Meanwhile, two other students are raising their hands and waiting for their turn. A girl is writing down everyone's ideas, and the teacher is listening quietly at the back.
Last semester, I spoke at a class meeting for the first time. We were choosing a place for our class trip, and I suggested a farm near our school because it was cheap and close. To my surprise, most of my classmates voted for my idea, and the trip was a great success. If I could decide how to use our class fund now, I would buy a bookshelf and some small plants. First, a bookshelf would help us keep our things in order. For example, we could put our dictionaries and test papers on it instead of on the floor. Second, plants would make our classroom greener and more relaxing. However, plants need care, so we would take turns watering them every day. In short, this plan would make our classroom a better place to study.

self_assessment.explanation_zh: 圖中的討論、自己的發言經驗和班費計畫都寫到，計畫有兩個理由與例子（內容 4）；先經驗後計畫，First、Second 讓理由清楚（組織 4）；過去式與 would 的用法正確，句型較簡單（文法句構 4）；用字正確但偏基礎（字彙拼字 3）。總分 15，屬穩健版。

model_texts.label: top
model_texts.text:
During the class meeting in the picture, the students are debating a question that matters to everyone: how should they spend the class fund? Standing beside the blackboard, the class leader is coordinating the discussion as chairperson, while the board behind him lists three options: new balls for PE class, an end-of-term party, or a bookshelf with some potted plants. In the front row, a boy has risen from his seat to explain his choice, and two classmates are already raising their hands, eager to respond. Judging from all those hands, the decision will not be an easy one. Off to the side, a girl is recording every suggestion in a notebook. Their homeroom teacher, meanwhile, is sitting quietly at the back, letting the students reach a consensus on their own.
I still remember the first time I spoke up at a class meeting. Last year, most of my classmates wanted to spend our trip money on an amusement park. Although my voice was shaking, I pointed out that the tickets alone would cost nearly half of our fund and suggested a farm nearby instead. When I finished listing the costs on the board, the room burst into applause, and the vote that followed was nearly unanimous. That day taught me that a good proposal needs clear numbers, not just strong feelings. This time, I would vote for the bookshelf and the plants. To begin with, a bookshelf would solve a daily problem: our dictionaries and test papers pile up on the floor, and at least two students trip over them every week. In addition, the plants would brighten the classroom and give us a shared responsibility, since everyone would take turns watering them. Admittedly, a party would be more exciting, but its joy would be fleeting, lasting only one afternoon. As a compromise, we could save a small part of the fund for a simple snack party at the end of the term. In conclusion, spending most of the money on things we use every day is the wiser choice.

notes.zh: 分詞片語補充說明；let＋人＋原形動詞

self_assessment.explanation_zh: 圖片描述完整，經驗段有數字與結果，計畫有具體問題、讓步與折衷方案（內容 5）；經驗帶出體會，再自然轉到計畫，結尾明確（組織 5）；問句、分詞片語、would 的假設用法正確多樣（文法句構 5）；applause、unanimous、compromise 用得貼切，但整體以常用字為主（字彙拼字 4）。總分 19，屬頂標版。

steady.comment_zh: 第一段主席、三個選項、發言與舉手的同學、做紀錄的同學與導師都寫到；第二段先寫第一次在班會發言、提議去農場的經驗，再用 If I could decide… 轉到買書架與盆栽的計畫，以 First／Second 列理由並舉例，補上輪流澆水，結構清楚、文法正確。句子多為簡單句，字彙偏基本；經驗和計畫之間沒有連結（沒寫出經驗帶來的體會），理由的說服力中等。

top.comment_zh: 第一段用 debating、coordinating the discussion as chairperson、eager to respond、reach a consensus 等精準用語寫出班會的氣氛；第二段經驗有細節（用門票費用說服同學、幾乎全票通過），並歸納出「好提案需要清楚的數字」，計畫以 To begin with／In addition 列兩個具體理由，讓步後提出折衷方案，結論明確。沒有語言錯誤。小瑕疵：從經驗轉到計畫的 This time, I would vote… 稍突然；圖中只有兩人舉手，all those hands 略誇張。

issues_zh: （參考，不影響判定）圖中站起來「發言」的同學和「做紀錄」的女生都畫成紅色（同批其他圖多用紅色代表女生），圖說卻寫發言的是男生，考生可能誤判性別。

steady.comment_zh: 第一段寫出主席、黑板上的三個選項、站起來發言與舉手等待的同學、記錄的女生和導師，完整清楚；第二段有第一次在班會發言（建議去農場）的經驗，再以 If I could decide 轉接提出書架與盆栽的計畫，附 First、Second 兩項理由。經驗部分略為簡短；文法正確，用字合宜（class fund、give his opinion、take turns）。

top.comment_zh: 第一段把主席、三個選項、發言與舉手的同學、記錄者與導師寫得完整又有氣氛；第二段以說明樂園門票費用而說服全班改去農場的經驗為例，帶出「好提案要有明確數字」的體悟，再提出書架與盆栽的計畫、兩項理由，並提出折衷方案。轉承自然、句型多變、用字精準，未見錯誤。「all those hands」略為誇大（圖中舉手的只有兩位），不影響評分。
